board.name: Tennessee Board of Physician Assistants (formerly the Committee on Physician Assistants of the Board of Medical Examiners)

notes.text: Programs must be approved by the AMA, AAPA or NCCPA.
NCCPA certified PAs report CE for their most recent NCCPA two-year period; others for the two-year period set by birth year.

window.reason: An NCCPA certified PA counts the most recent NCCPA two-year period; others the two-year period set by birth year. Neither is the license expiration, so the member sets CME Cycle Start to that period's first day.

agreement.text: A written protocol signed by the PA and supervising physician is kept at the practice location and reviewed at least every two years; the board is told of a change in primary supervising physician within 15 days.

dated.item: Board target for the collaborative practice endorsement rules (6,000 postgraduate hours); recheck the Tennessee PA practice agreement

options.text: At least two items from the board's competence list each renewal period: for example a satisfactory employer or peer evaluation, contract renewal, a written self-evaluation, specialty certification, or 10 contact hours of continuing education (one item)

ce.reason: APRN competence at renewal is current national certification plus one additional item from the RN competence list.

options.text: Current national certification, plus one more item from the RN competence list (for example 10 contact hours of continuing education, or a satisfactory employer evaluation)

agreement.text: A prescribing APRN has a collaborating physician and files a notice naming that physician and the formulary before prescribing. Protocols are reviewed and updated biennially, and the physician reviews at least 20% of charts every 30 days.
